correctness.rationale: For every 3<=m<=n over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the source defines P as the reduced closure of jets at nonzero rank-one X, rather than the entire reducible jet scheme. Košir–Sethuraman supply the prime ideal (2x2 minors of X, their X/Y polarizations, 3x3 minors of Y). The nonzero-X locus is a smooth rank-(m+n-1) tangent bundle; dimension=2(m+n-1). On rank Y=2, the pivot A, Schur complement D-CA^(-1)B and Y-dependent invertible row/column operations set Y to diag(I_2,0) scheme-theoretically. The polarized minors then set all X entries outside the leading 2x2 block to zero and force its trace zero; the remaining X minor is a^2+bc=0. Free rank-two-Y coordinates number 2(m+n-2), and the transverse quadratic cone has isolated A1 singularity and multiplicity 2. Every lower-Y-rank point of the zero-X fiber is singular by closedness/density; no X!=0 point is singular. The reduced singular support is exactly X=0,rank(Y)<=2, irreducible dimension 2(m+n-2), codimension 2. Prime domain plus Jonov Cohen–Macaulay S2 and R1 gives normality. Original finite verifier checks 20 tangent ranks modulo 101 only; these are not an infinite proof.
residual_risks: Global Jacobian singular subscheme, rank(Y)<=1 local types and positive characteristic are not determined; theorem is reduced and characteristic zero.
Prime ideal and Cohen–Macaulay are correctly cited external inputs, not freshly reproved results.

value.rationale: The reduced principal jet component of a determinantal cone is a standard natural geometric object. Exact codimension-two singular support, a uniform A1 transverse chart for every matrix size and normality distinguish intrinsic singularities from the known reducibility of the total jet scheme. They are substantive scheme-level and divisor-theoretic geometry, not a textbook reuse of CM or an isolated finite numerical check.
